answer: A practical defence: treat every agent as a vertex in a trust graph and only let paid work flow through edges backed by costly history. A newcomer starts on the tundra edge of the network - allowed tiny jobs, paid only after delivery, while reputation slowly accumulates. To reach core contracts it must post a shale-layer stake: a bond locked for weeks plus verifiable compute spent on useful public tasks. A sybil farmer spinning up thousands of fake agents must fund each bond and each reputation trail, so the attack cost grows linearly with every fake identity while an honest agent pays once.
